authoringPass.driftDisclosure:
LEADER-SIDE FREEZE EVENTS, self-reported. Two kinds occurred and they are recorded separately because they differ in consequence.

KIND 1 -- a hashed operand moved while a gate was open. This happened at pass 9 and at pass 15. In both, review lanes were mid-read when an operand byte changed, so the digest those lanes hashed no longer matched disk and their sourceHash binding was void. Pass 15 invalidated four already-running pass-14 lanes (2088 cleaner, 2089 QA, 2090 architect, 2091 critic); their findings were treated as input rather than as gate verdicts, and the pass-14 H3 bytes they hashed are not on disk, so those four verdicts cannot be re-adjudicated against what they actually read. The pass-11 rule that forbids this is the authoring lane's own.

KIND 2, mid-read H5 edits, stated as a rule because every numeral this field has carried went stale at the next pass. THE RULE: every pass from 23 onward has edited H5 while at least one lane of the in-flight gate was still reading. No count is given. Two earlier wordings here gave one -- 'third', and an enumeration of passes 23 and 24 -- and both were already stale when written, because passes 25 and 26 were themselves mid-read edits and the pass-24 cleaner and critic lanes were reading through them (pass-24 cleaner lane, carried forward by IRC). The pass authoring this sentence is authoringPass.pass, so a reader can derive the span without a maintained list. This is milder than KIND 1 in one specific respect and no other: H5 carries no frozen digest and is not an argv operand, so no lane's sourceHash was invalidated. It is still not harmless -- H5 is in every lane's read set, so a finding about H5 prose can be stale against later bytes, and lanes have been told to rebind rather than yield against superseded text. What IS true of every pass from 16 onward, and checkable without prose: none moved a hashed operand. digestSetsByPass records an empty entry for each such pass, and the five operand digests in the files map have not changed since pass 15.
authoringPass.digestSetsByPassNote: Changed-file delta log, NOT a snapshot series. Only passes 1, 2 and 3 record all five hashed operands; every pass from 4 onward records only the operands whose digest moved in that pass, and every pass from 16 onward records none, because each of those passes edited H5 alone and H5 is not a hashed operand. An earlier version of this note called the map a per-pass snapshot with three delta exceptions (passes 4, 6, 8); that was wrong -- passes 5, 7, 9, 10, 11, 12, 13, 14 and 15 are partial too. It also claimed some entries repeat a prior digest because a file went untouched; no (operand, digest) pair repeats across any two passes at all, which follows from it being a delta log. The pass-11 critic raised this as F7, the pass-15 QA lane raised it again as O3, and it is now described as what it is.

Pass 9 asserted in H2 that 'a symlink aimed outside the repo is rejected instead of silently copied in'. FALSE as implemented -- canonicalization resolved the directory only, never the leaf. Proven false by executable test: a symlink at sub/evil.sql aimed outside was accepted and read SECRET-OUTSIDE-REPO. Fixed by full-path realpath plus returning the canonical value; the same test now rejects it.

Pass 9 asserted the verification gates touched 'no file outside the authored set'. Contradicted by this artifact's own liveEvidenceObtained, which records synthetic /tmp fixtures. Withdrawn and filed under stateDeltaBreachesAndDisclosureGaps.

Pass 10 claimed via H1 that the post-copy check proved the two files 'are the two expected ones'. An ls -1 name count cannot show that -- a wrong-source or truncated copy satisfies it identically. Withdrawn and replaced with an in-container digest comparison against the host source.

Pass 11 recorded as live evidence that 'a missing file yields an empty digest caught by the -n guard'. True only WITHOUT pipefail, which is not how the launcher runs. The guard was unreachable and || fail was the actual catcher. Withdrawn; the guards are now structurally reachable and re-verified.

Pass 13 asserted in H3's A4 rationale that a five- or seven-column function would 'still pass' the name and type vectors. That was false -- both compare against fixed six-element targets. Withdrawn in pass 14 and replaced with the narrower true claim, including an explicit statement that the mode assertion's per-element comparison is tautological. The overclaim was mine and it was introduced by the very fix that closed the dead-output blocker, which is the recurring hazard this ledger exists to catch.

Pass 14 asserted in H3's A4 comment that the mode assertion is 'the only check in A4 that fails closed on NULL proargmodes'. Withdrawn as false: the name check fails closed on the same input because both arrays come from one aggregation. The claim was found by the authoring lane's own probe, not by a review lane.

Pass 14 asserted in H3's A4 comment, as the mechanism behind the NULL case, that 'a scalar-returning function has NULL proargmodes, the LATERAL unnest yields zero rows'. Withdrawn as false ON THE PADDED SHAPE ONLY -- it remains the operative mechanism for the both-NULL shape, as stated below. A multi-argument unnest pads to the LONGEST argument, so the behaviour depends on the co-argument. Named-argument function: unnest(proargmodes, proargnames) emits one row per name with NULL in the padded am column, and WHERE s.am = 't' is what empties the set -- so the withdrawn wording named the wrong cause. Unnamed-argument or zero-argument set-returning function: both arrays are NULL, unnest(NULL, NULL) yields zero rows, and the withdrawn wording is correct there. Pass 16 stated the padding replacement as an unqualified absolute, which was itself wrong (QA lane, pass 16); this label and this body are both scoped. The fail-closed conclusion holds on every shape: array_agg over zero rows returns NULL and NULL IS DISTINCT FROM the six-element literal fires. This label was double-spliced at pass 19 by two patch scripts both targeting it, producing duplicated qualifier text; rewritten once here (cleaner lane, pass 19, blocker 1).

RepoDigests entries are TAGLESS on this host: ["supabase/postgres@sha256:ac581882..."]. Matching a tag-bearing form could never succeed and would have aborted the launcher before docker create.

The H4 scanner was executed over synthetic fixture trees under /tmp with python3 -B, never pointed at the repository tree. Cases exercised and matched: two clean files; a bare forbidden literal reported with file, line and literal; a line-initial '--' comment skipped; an indented '--' comment skipped; a '/* */' region skipped; a MID-LINE '--' followed by a literal CAUGHT rather than skipped; uppercase G026 matched as a case-distinct member; a literal after '*/' caught; an absent scan-set member exiting non-zero with a message that names no literal and no line number; and per-file attribution correct in both directions.

ONE CASE IS NOT 'as specified' and the earlier head sentence here wrongly counted it among them. An unterminated '/*' sets the in-block flag and blanks every remaining line to EOF, so a forbidden literal after it is NOT reported and the scan exits 0. That is fail-OPEN, the opposite direction from the mid-line '--' decision, which H4's own note defends as fail-closed. The frozen rule names a region between '/*' and '*/'; an unterminated opener closes no region, so treating it as comment-to-EOF is a permissive reading rather than a requirement. Found by the pass-22 QA lane (O5) and re-confirmed by execution at pass 24.

It is filed in openForPhase2b rather than asserted here (pass-24 QA lane, O-P24-8).
